english: The boat was going on the sea. Then the rain-clouds covered the sky, and the darkness became thick. Then Perkʷunos gave thunder. The sea became agitated, and the water was swelling. Then the men became afraid. The rope broke. The boat was splitting. Then the leader cried out, "Perkʷunos, rescue us!" Then they threw the silver into the sea. Then the thunder went away, and the rain-clouds went away. It dawned. They were alive.

english: Mother Earth, I shall lie down. Mother Earth, guard me in the night. Now, stars, look at me! May the beast not eat me up; may sleep take me. May my horses lie beside me. May the night cover me; may the fire be burning. Dawn, may I wake in your light.

english: A wolf came to a shepherd. "Sell me a sheep!" "I shall sell you one." Then he clothed the dog in wool. The wolf gave a wild bull and took the dog. He did not recognize the dog. Then the wolf, carrying the dog, was going to the hill, and he became joyful. Then the dog seized the wolf and was tearing him. He cried out and fled. The shepherd drove the bull to the home. Whoever deceives is deceived.

english: The stranger and the horse were going along the way. The sun was heating the two. They were thirsty, and they were sweating. They were seeking water, and they did not find it. Then the horse went forward, and the stranger followed it. They came to water. It was broad. Then the horse drank, and the stranger was drinking the water. Then the stranger sat down. Then they were satisfied. Whoever is thirsty, to him water is dear.

english: It dawned. Then the man stood up and put on footwear. Then he took gifts. His mother was cooking. Then he harnessed the two swift horses. Then his wife said to him, "Go, and return unharmed." Then his father said, "May the gods guard you!" Then he went out of the home, and the dog followed him. The sun came forth. The wheel of the sun was high. A bird was going ahead. Then he saw the long path. The path was long, and he did not become afraid. He was seeking great fame.

english: The shepherd was sitting at the enclosure. A man came to him. He said, "I give you four cattle. Give me ten sheep!" The shepherd said, "The sheep are many. Let us make a pledge. Whoever breaks the pledge, may the gods slay him!" Then the shepherd got four cattle by trade, and the man got ten sheep by trade. The man drove the sheep away. The shepherd drove them into the enclosure. The two became joyful.

english: A stranger came by the path. The man saw him and stood up. The stranger said, "Where are you going?" The man said, "I am going home. My home is far. Who are you?" "I am a stranger." "What is your name?" "My name is famous." "I do not know it." Then the two sat down together. The stranger gave him water, and they ate. Then the stranger said, "May the gods lead you!" And he went away. The man went forward.

english: For ten years the king of good fame did not see the home. Then he came, and he was a stranger. The wife saw him, and she did not recognize him. She gave him water, and he drank it. He said, "I have seen the king." "Where have you seen him?" "I have seen him on the sea. He is alive." "He is alive?" "He will return unharmed." "May the gods lead him!" Then he said, "I am the king. My name is famous." The wife looked at him, and her heart knew him. Then her tears came forth.

english: The trader and the master made a pledge. Then the master gave five horses. Then the trader took the horses. He did not give the silver. "Where is the silver?" "The horses are not swift!" Then the master said, "Whoever breaks the pledge, Father Sky, strike him!" Then thunder came forth. And the home of the trader burned. Then he became afraid. He gave it to the master. The pledge stood.

english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, come to me! You who drive the stars away; you who lead the wheel of the sun; you who are red; be bright on my path! Dawn, be bright on my horses! Dawn, bring light to me! Dawn, may my heart become joyful. Dawn, lead me to my home. Dawn, may I see your light.

english: The sea is great. The rivers go to the sea. The sea is not filled. Fish live in the sea. Beasts do not live in the sea. No one ploughs the sea. There is no path on the sea. The boat is a path. The star points out the path to the boat. The sun sinks in the sea. Dawn, the daughter of Sky, becomes bright. The sea is dear to the fish. The sea gives men fish and death. Great is the sea.

english: The way was long, and the hills were high. It was winter. Then the man was climbing the height. Snow lay on the hills. It became cold. His breath came forth, and he became tired. Then he saw a wolf. The beast was standing in the snow and kept looking at him. Then the man threw a stone, and the wolf fled. Then he sat down and ate, and leaned against the stone. It became warm, and the snow melted. Then he saw the distant river. Then he went down.

Then she gave it to him, and he gave her silver, and she took it. Then the two became joyful. Then the trader bought much wool and carried it away. He sold it and took much silver. The trader became rich.

english: A father and his son came to the water. The father said, "River goddess, you are swift! We give you a poured gift." Then he put the gift into the water. "Let us cross. Do not kill us!" The son trembled. It listened to them. Then the two crossed, and the water did not seize them. Then they stood on the other side. The father said, "The river goddess is unfailing."

english: It was getting dark. Then the man sat down on the earth, and his two heels became tired. Then he prepared a fire. The fire was burning. It became cold. Then many stars shone. The night was long, and the darkness was thick. He was looking at the stars. "Stars, do you see my home?" The stars did not speak. "I remember my home." "Mother Earth, protect me!" The fire became slack. Then sleep seized him. Then it dawned, and the wheel of the sun came forth. Then he woke up and stood up.

He saw the great water. Then he said, "I shall not cross. I shall build a shelter." Then he lay down in the shelter and ate. The thunder went away, and the rain-clouds went away. Then it dawned, and the water was not great. The sun became bright. Then he crossed it.

english: Two men came to the river. A boat-man was sitting there. Then they said, "Boat-man, carry us to the other side!" Then he said, "What will you give me?" "We shall give silver." "Sit down in the boat!" Then they gave it, and sat down in the boat. "Do not be afraid!" The boat-man drove the boat. The water was broad. Then the boat-man drove the boat forward. Then they stood on the other side. They said, "May the gods give you good things!"

english: A stranger who was buying came to the master of the wool. He said, "Your wool is not good!" The master said, "It is good. Look at it!" "It is not good. It is not good! I shall go away." "Do not go away! I shall give it to you." "What is the price?" "The price is not high." Then he gave silver and took it. Then he went away. Then he came again, and bought more wool.

english: There was darkness on the sea, and many stars shone. The boat was going. The leader kept looking at a star. Those stars were going around; that star stood. He said, "Star, lead us! We are confident." The boat followed the star. Then the sky was red. Then Dawn came, and the star went away. The sea became bright.

pie: awis akwabʰyams ā wawakat: kard agʰnutai mai widanti manum akwams agantam.
english: The sheep said to the horses: "My heart pains me, seeing a man driving horses."

pie: h₂ówis h₁éḱwōs-kʷe
english: The Sheep and the Horses

pie: wesowiHrós h₁éḱwons yéwgt. nu dʰéh₁t h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m kʷékʷloy. nu dweh₂róh₁ stigʰéh₁ gʷéh₂t. déh₂nuh₂ bʰérǵʰons-kʷe pr̥wé. nu h₁ludʰét kʷelséh₂m dʰéǵʰōm. gʰóstis h₂én h₁ést. ǵʰiméni h₂én tḱéyt. nu h₂wĺ̥h₁neh₂m pérh₂t kʷrinéh₂t-kʷe h₂ŕ̥ǵn̥tom pĺ̥h₂seh₂m márkom-kʷe. nu pĺ̥h₂seh₂m wóǵʰoy dʰéh₁t. nu nést. h₁ésyo pótn̥yeh₂ey pĺ̥h₂seh₂m déh₃t. bʰúHt h₁ésyo h₁nómn̥ ḱlutóm.
english: The trader harnessed the horses. Then he put the wool into the wagon. Then he went by the long path. He crossed rivers and hills. Then he arrived at the distant earth. There he was a stranger. In winter he dwelt there. He sold the wool and bought silver, a woman's garment and a horse. Then he put the garment into the wagon. Then he returned unharmed. He gave the garment to his wife. His name became famous.

pie: h₂eǵós kʷékʷlom h₂éǵet duktā́m-kʷe HéHḱuh₁ dwóh₁ h₁éḱwoh₁ h₁ím. nu rótos Hrumptó. h₁éḱwōs sth₂éh₁yont. nu sédt h₂eǵós wérh₁t-kʷe. kʷís rótom démēti? nu tétḱō gʷémt. skidtóm rótom widéh₁yet. h₂éǵt. rótom démōh₂. misdʰóm moy h₁opéye. h₁áyt h₂eǵós h₁ésmey misdʰóm. tétḱō wr̥ǵyét rótom-kʷe démet h₂linéHt-kʷe h₁ím sm̥réwh₁. nu yugóm h₂réydʰet. nu h₂eǵós kʷékʷlom h₂ew h₂éǵet. tetḱnés h₃épos h₁wésu h₁ésti.
english: The driver was driving the wagon, and the two swift horses were pulling it. Then the wheel broke. The horses were standing still. The driver sat down and said, "Who will build a wheel?" Then a carpenter came. He saw the split wheel. He said, "I shall build a wheel. Give me a wage!" The driver gave him a wage. The carpenter was working, and he built the wheel, and smeared it with grease. Then he set the yoke in order. Then the driver drove the wagon again. The work of the carpenter is good.

pie: h₂érh₃yet swésōr h₂éǵroy. nu wiHrós stigʰéh₁ gʷm̥sḱét. h₁ím ne spéḱyet. nu h₂wéyst swésōr h₁ésyo gʷéh₂mn̥ h₁íd-kʷe ǵnéh₃t. h₁ésyeh₂s ḱḗr trémt. HréwdHt bʰréh₂ter. nu h₂éǵrom linkʷn̥tíh₂ swésōr drémt. bʰréh₂tēr sékʷt. nésm̥ swésor. wéwket. lewbʰós h₁ési. nu dṓm ih₂tā́m.
english: The sister was ploughing in the field. A man was walking along the path. She did not look at him. Then the sister heard his step, and she knew it. Her heart trembled. She cried out, "Brother!" Then the sister, leaving the field, ran. The brother said, "Sister, I returned unharmed." She said, "Dear are you!" Then the two went home.

pie: gʰóstis bʰérǵʰoy sédyontm̥ poh₂iménm̥ widéh₁yet. nu h₁ésmey sékʷt. wódr̥ kúdʰe h₁ésti? nu wéwket poh₂imḗn. h₁íd h₂én h₁ésti stóygʰom-kʷe déyḱet. ní gʷh₂dʰí h₂éǵrom-kʷe pr̥dʰí. nu h₁íd widḗsi. nu gʰóstis bʰéh₂t. stóygʰos dweh₂rós h₁ésti? stóygʰos dweh₂rós ne h₁ésti. deywṓs te h₂léksoyh₁ent. nu gʷéh₂t gʰóstis ní.
english: The stranger saw a sitting shepherd on the hill. He said to him, "Where is the water?" The shepherd said, "It is yonder." And he pointed out the path. "Go down, and cross the field. Then you will see it." The stranger said, "Is the way long?" "The way is not long. May the gods protect you." Then the stranger went down.
